findings.summary: An int literal in one branch of an if-expression is not lifted to Mod when the other branch is Mod, so `if c: 0 else: cb.choose(a, b)` fails with E0302.
findings.evidence: type Z = Mod<1_000_000_007>; let cb = Comb<Z>(10); print(if true: 0 else: cb.choose(3, 1))  -> error[E0302]: expected `Int`, found `Mod<1000000007>`

findings.summary: `scan(a, +)` returns a Prefix that is not a Seq, so `.min()` and `inversions()` reject it and the running sum becomes a manual push loop.
findings.evidence: use std.seq.*; let s = scan([1, -2, 3], +); print(s.min()) -> error[E0203]: Prefix<Int, Int> has no field or method `min`; inversions(s) -> error[E0606]. Wanted: `let s = a.scan(+)` then `s.min()`, `inversions(s)`; wrote `var s: List<Int> = []; var run = 0; for x in a: run += x; s.push(run)`

findings.summary: Default `cpl stress` generator for `let (n, m) = read(); let (s, t): (Str, Str) = read()` makes strings unrelated to n/m (n=149108 with a 7-char string), so I had to write a @gen.

findings.summary: Under @!multitest a @gen must print the test count itself; omitting it gives only `the brute ... failed on this input (Code(3))` with no hint.
findings.evidence: @gen printing `n m / s / t` without a leading `1` -> `error: the brute cf2272E.cp (\`brute\`) failed on this input (Code(3)), so there is nothing to compare with`

findings.summary: `['R', 'W'].join("")` type-checks and prints an empty line: join is called on the separator, and a List<Char> silently passes as a Str separator, while `["ab"].join(",")` is a clear type error.
findings.evidence: `print(['R', 'W'].join(""))` prints `` (empty); `print(['R', 'W'])` prints `RW`; `print(["ab", "c"].join(","))` -> error[E0302] help: `join` is called on the separator

findings.summary: Move checking is not applied inside @check: `var b = a` in a loop compiles there, while the same code in the solution is error[E0608] as the ownership spec says.
findings.evidence: design/p9.cp (@check with `for i in 0..3: var b = a`) -> `cpl check`: no errors; design/p8.cp (same loop in main) -> `error[E0608]: \`a\` moves here in one round of the loop, so the next round finds it already moved`
